title: Platform Overview
summary: A guide to Blastrr's simulated markets, platform specifications, and trading architecture.

groups.title: Welcome to Blastrr
paragraphs: Blastrr is a simulated perpetual futures trading and performance evaluation platform giving traders access to digital asset, FX, index, and commodity markets in a simulated environment.

The platform combines synthetic liquidity and market spreads with simulated leverage, testnet settlement, and performance reward workflows. All account balances, orders, and positions use simulated funds; users do not risk personal trading capital through simulated trades.

groups.title: What You Can Trade
paragraphs: Markets use a unified execution and cross-margin system, allowing positions across supported asset classes to share account collateral. Availability varies by market and account.
items: Digital assets: BTC, ETH, SOL, LUN, and supported crypto perpetual pairs, available continuously.
Forex: supported major and minor currency pairs during their market sessions.
Commodities: supported metals and energy markets, including Gold (XAU), Silver (XAG), and Crude Oil (WTI).
Indices: supported benchmark markets, including S&P 500 (US500) and Nasdaq 100 (US100).
See Trading Markets for market availability shown in the terminal.

groups.title: Trading Architecture
items: Unified cross margin: usable simulated account equity supports eligible open positions across markets.
Simulated collateral: supported testnet balances are used for simulated trading.
Real-time updates: order fills, floating PnL, and balance changes are reflected in the simulated account.
Automated risk controls: applicable loss limits and drawdown rules are monitored by the platform.

groups.title: Blastrr Capital
paragraphs: Blastrr Capital is the platform's simulated funded account and performance evaluation program. Current account availability and rules are described in Blastrr Capital Overview, Account Tiers, and Loss Limits & Risk Enforcement.
items: Straight-to-funded plans provide simulated funded account access after checkout confirmation.
Eligible performance reward requests are subject to account rules, risk review, and verification.
No simulated performance result guarantees a real-world payment or financial return.

groups.title: Web3 and Account Access

title: Trading Markets
summary: Market coverage, continuous crypto trading, leverage caps, and market discovery.

groups.title: Market Coverage
paragraphs: Blastrr provides simulated perpetual markets. The Markets list in the Trading Terminal is the current source for active symbols and availability.
items: Major digital assets: BTC/USD, ETH/USD, SOL/USD, and LUN/USD where listed.
Additional crypto markets may include assets such as AVAX, NEAR, ARB, SUI, LINK, UNI, AAVE, and TIA. Availability can change.
Other asset classes, including forex, commodities, and indices, are available only where shown as active in the terminal.

groups.title: Trading Schedule
paragraphs: Crypto perpetual markets are designed for continuous 24/7/365 trading. Platform maintenance or service interruptions may temporarily affect access. Other asset classes may follow their applicable session schedules.

groups.title: Leverage Caps

items: Primary demo accounts may have higher leverage limits than Blastrr Capital accounts.
Blastrr Capital crypto leverage is limited according to the market and account risk rules.
Changing leverage changes required margin; it does not change the nominal dollar PnL of an unchanged position size.

title: Order Types
summary: Market and limit orders, time in force, reduce-only controls, and conditional TP/SL orders.

groups.title: Supported Order Types
items: Market order: requests immediate simulated execution against available market liquidity. The fill price may differ from the displayed price.
Limit order: sets a maximum buy price or minimum sell price. Execution depends on the market reaching the order price and available liquidity.
Stop-Limit or other conditional orders: available only where shown in the terminal; the stop trigger and resulting order behavior depend on the selected order configuration.

groups.title: Time in Force
paragraphs: Time in force controls how long an unfilled order remains active. Options shown may vary by order type.

rows: Executes available quantity immediately and cancels any remainder.
Executes the full quantity immediately or cancels the order.
Rejects an order that would immediately execute as a taker, where supported.

groups.title: Reduce Only
paragraphs: Reduce Only orders are intended to decrease or close an existing position. They should not increase or reverse the position. The platform may reject an order if it would not reduce the current position.

groups.title: Take Profit and Stop Loss
items: Take Profit (TP) can trigger a closing order when a selected price condition is met.
Stop Loss (SL) can trigger a closing order when a selected loss boundary is reached.
Where available, TP/SL can be set during order entry or adjusted on an open position.
Trigger execution depends on the selected trigger and order type, available liquidity, and current platform conditions.

groups.title: Execution and Risk Indicators
paragraphs: Orders execute against the platform's simulated market and order book. Limit orders may fill partially; market execution can be affected by liquidity and simulated slippage.
Review the order ticket's Fail Price or liquidation indicator when available. It is an estimate of a risk boundary, not a guarantee of the eventual execution price.

title: Cross Margin & Leverage
summary: How simulated margin, position sizing, market leverage caps, and portfolio risk work.

groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: Eligible Blastrr accounts use cross margin backed by simulated collateral. Usable account equity can support multiple open positions rather than being isolated to one market. All balances, positions, and executions remain simulated.

groups.title: Margin and Position Sizing
paragraphs: Margin is the portion of simulated equity required to support a position. Leverage increases the notional exposure supported by a given margin amount and magnifies both simulated gains and losses.

Notional Value = Position Quantity × Simulated Mark Price
Estimated Initial Margin = Notional Value ÷ Selected Leverage
Changing leverage affects margin requirements for new orders; it does not change the dollar PnL of an unchanged position size.

groups.title: Leverage Limits
paragraphs: Maximum leverage is market- and account-dependent. Primary demo accounts and Blastrr Capital accounts may have different caps. Use the order ticket for current allowed leverage.
items: Blastrr Capital accounts use lower leverage caps than some demo markets.
Caps can vary between major and more volatile crypto pairs.
Temporary Leverage Limits may further reduce limits during specified events.

groups.title: Unified Cross Margin
paragraphs: Usable simulated collateral supports eligible open positions. Portfolio equity reflects collateral and realized and floating PnL, subject to platform accounting and transfers.
Effective Portfolio Leverage = Total Notional Value of Open Positions ÷ Portfolio Equity
Cross margin can allow profits in one position to offset losses in another, but it also exposes shared account equity to losses across open positions.

groups.title: Margin Requirements and Liquidation
paragraphs: New orders require sufficient available equity to meet initial margin requirements. If equity falls below applicable maintenance requirements, the platform may liquidate positions. Blastrr Capital loss limits can invalidate an account independently of ordinary margin requirements.

groups.title: Risk on Blastrr Capital Accounts
items: Daily Loss Limit checks account equity, including applicable floating PnL, against the daily floor.
Maximum Drawdown checks equity against the account's fixed drawdown floor.
Leverage and position size affect how quickly market movements can approach these risk boundaries.

title: Funding Rates
summary: What simulated funding represents, how payments affect positions, and how to view current rates.

groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: Funding is a simulated transfer between long and short holders, not a platform trading fee. Funding mechanisms are used in perpetual futures to help keep a contract price aligned with a reference market.
When funding is positive, long holders generally pay short holders. When funding is negative, short holders generally pay long holders. Funding payments adjust simulated position equity.

groups.title: Settlement Frequency
paragraphs: Funding intervals can vary by market and platform configuration. Check the current rate and next settlement timing displayed in the trading terminal; do not rely on a fixed interval from this guide.

groups.title: Funding Rate Components
paragraphs: Funding calculations may use the premium between synthetic execution prices and a reference index, alongside an interest component and configured clamps. Exact inputs and intervals may change by market.
Premium Index = (Buy Impact Price Premium − Sell Impact Price Premium) ÷ Index Price
The supplied crypto specification describes: I = Annual Interest Rate × H ÷ (365 × 24), and Hourly Funding Rate = [P + clamp(I − P, −K × I, +K × I)] ÷ H.

In this model, P is the average premium index, I is the interval interest rate, H is the normalization interval, and K is the clamp multiplier. The supplied example parameters are a 10.95% annual interest rate, H = 24 hours, and K = 1.
The platform's displayed funding rate is the source of truth for the applicable market and settlement period.

groups.title: Funding Payment Example
paragraphs: Funding Payment = Position Notional × Funding Rate.
For example, a $1,000,000 simulated position at a 0.00375% hourly funding rate would produce a $37.50 simulated payment for that hour. The paying side depends on the funding direction.
This is an illustration, not a quoted rate or settlement schedule. Use the rate and next settlement timing displayed in the terminal.

groups.title: How Funding Affects Risk
items: Funding credits or debits affect floating position equity.
A large funding payment can change an account's distance from its Daily Loss Limit or Maximum Drawdown floor.
Review funding information in the terminal before holding a position through a settlement.

title: Temporary Leverage Limits
summary: How temporary leverage restrictions may affect new orders, resting orders, and open positions.

groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: During periods of extreme volatility, reduced liquidity, major market events, or infrastructure maintenance, Blastrr may temporarily lower leverage limits on selected markets. Any active restriction and its scope should be confirmed from current platform notices and order ticket settings.

groups.title: When a Limit Activates
items: New orders may remain available but are subject to the temporary leverage cap.
Unfilled orders that exceed an applicable reduced limit may be cancelled or rejected.
The handling of open positions depends on the announced event rules, account equity, and current platform risk controls.
Attached TP/SL controls may remain active, subject to platform position changes and order behavior.

paragraphs: The source material gives the following examples for Blastrr Capital accounts. They are illustrative only; active restrictions may differ and are announced through current platform notices and order ticket settings.

groups.title: When a Limit Ends
paragraphs: When a temporary restriction is removed, ordinary market and account limits may resume. Orders cancelled during an event may need to be submitted again. Check platform notices and current order settings.

groups.title: Managing Positions During an Event
items: Monitor available collateral and account equity.
Consider reducing leverage or position size before a scheduled restriction takes effect.
Review open orders and TP/SL settings after any market or position adjustment.

title: Deposits & Testnet Collateral
summary: Provisioning simulated balances, faucet access, and troubleshooting balance updates.

groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: Primary demo workspaces may use virtual testnet collateral such as USDT, USDC, or LUN. These balances are simulated and are not a deposit of live trading capital.
Blastrr Capital simulated funded accounts are provisioned according to account setup and do not accept user deposits.

groups.title: Ways to Provision a Demo Balance
items: Use the Faucet, Reset Balance, or Top-Up control shown in the dashboard when available.
Wallet-based testnet features and supported networks depend on your account and the active platform configuration.
Never send real tokens to a simulated faucet or an address not explicitly provided for a supported transaction.

groups.title: Minimums and Availability
paragraphs: Faucet amounts, request limits, minimums, and supported networks can change. Follow the controls and instructions shown in the platform.

groups.title: Balance Troubleshooting
items: Check whether a Process Faucet or synchronization action is available in the dashboard.
Refresh your session after allowing any displayed network confirmation time.
If needed, disconnect and reconnect your wallet, then confirm the selected network.
If the balance still does not update, contact support through the platform widget or the official support channel.

title: Withdrawals
summary: Distinguish wallet transfers from performance claims and review transfer steps and status.

groups.title: Claim Profit vs. Withdrawal
paragraphs: A Claim Profit request moves eligible simulated performance rewards from a Blastrr Capital account to the user's Primary Account, subject to review.

A withdrawal or wallet transfer moves an available balance from a Primary Account to an external wallet. These are separate flows with different eligibility, verification, processing, and network requirements.

groups.title: Processing and Networks
paragraphs: Processing times and supported networks depend on the transaction and current platform conditions. Review the withdrawal panel for the latest supported networks, asset, fees, limits, and estimated timing.

groups.title: How to Withdraw
items: Open the Withdraw control from the appropriate account view.
Enter or select the destination public wallet address and choose a supported network.
Enter the amount and review the asset, destination, network, and any displayed fees or limits.
Confirm only after verifying the details. On-chain transfers may be irreversible.

groups.title: Limits and Verification
paragraphs: Minimum amounts, rolling limits, security reviews, and identity checks can depend on account status and current platform policy. The supplied documentation describes a 1 USDT minimum and a 50,000 USDT rolling 24-hour transfer threshold, with larger requests subject to additional review. Confirm current requirements in the withdrawal panel.

groups.title: Track a Transfer
items: Use the Withdrawals or Claims history in your dashboard to review type, asset, amount, status, date, and transaction reference when available.
If a transfer appears complete but has not arrived, inspect its transaction reference on the relevant block explorer, then contact support with the transaction details.

title: Blastrr Capital Overview
summary: Straight-to-funded simulated accounts, their shared rules, and reward eligibility.

groups.title: Program Overview
paragraphs: Blastrr Capital provides Straight-to-Funded simulated accounts. Accounts are provisioned as simulated funded profiles after checkout confirmation; there are no evaluation stages in the current plan structure.

All balances, orders, and positions are simulated. Funded status does not represent live trading capital or guarantee a real-world payment. Reward requests are subject to current terms, risk review, and verification.

groups.title: What the Program Provides
items: Simulated capital assigned to the selected plan.
A shared trading interface and eligible crypto perpetual market access.
Account-specific leverage limits and risk boundaries.
The ability to submit eligible performance reward requests, subject to account rules.

groups.title: Risk Rules
paragraphs: Current Straight-to-Funded plans use a 5% Daily Loss Limit and a 10% static Maximum Drawdown, plus a 40% single-day profit consistency rule for reward claims. See Account Tiers and Loss Limits & Risk Enforcement for details.

groups.title: Account Management
items: Account caps, available markets, leverage, and claim eligibility are governed by current platform rules.
Account access fee policies and refund eligibility are displayed during checkout and in the current terms.
Claim Profit and external wallet withdrawals are separate account flows.

title: Blastrr Capital Account Tiers
summary: Current Straight-to-Funded capital tiers and their shared risk and consistency parameters.

groups.title: Straight-to-Funded Plans
paragraphs: Blastrr Capital currently offers Straight-to-Funded simulated accounts. Accounts are provisioned after checkout confirmation. No evaluation or multi-step challenge is required.
The table lists account parameters, not purchase pricing. Current checkout and platform rules remain authoritative.

groups.title: Universal Tier Parameters
items: Daily Loss Limit: 5% of starting daily equity, resetting at 00:00 UTC. Applicable equity checks include floating PnL.
Maximum Drawdown: fixed static floor calculated from initial starting capital at 10%.
Profit consistency: at claim time, no single trading day may account for more than 40% of total net virtual profit.
Crypto execution: available crypto perpetuals are intended to trade continuously, subject to platform availability and maintenance.

title: Loss Limits & Risk Enforcement
summary: Daily loss floors, static drawdown, account invalidation, and pre-trade risk indicators.

groups.title: Standard Risk Parameters
paragraphs: Straight-to-Funded Blastrr Capital accounts use two continuously monitored risk boundaries: a 5% Daily Loss Limit and a 10% static Maximum Drawdown. Values below are based on the stated starting simulated capital.

headers: Daily Equity Floor at Starting Balance

groups.title: Maximum Drawdown (10% Static Floor)
paragraphs: The Maximum Drawdown is a static dollar floor set from the account's initial simulated capital. It does not trail high-water equity or move up with profits.
Static Floor = Initial Capital − (Initial Capital × 10%)
If account equity, including applicable floating PnL, reaches the floor, the account may be invalidated under current risk rules.

groups.title: Daily Loss Limit (5% Daily Reset)
paragraphs: The Daily Loss Limit resets at 00:00 UTC. The reset balance is captured according to platform accounting rules. Floating equity is monitored against the daily floor.
Daily Equity Floor = Reset Balance × 0.95 + Net Transfers Since Reset
Intraday profits do not raise that day's floor; the floor is recalculated at the next reset. Applicable transfers may adjust the floor.

groups.title: Breach Handling
paragraphs: Touching or crossing an applicable risk floor can result in immediate account invalidation. The system may cancel pending orders and close open positions. Follow the current account rules; do not assume there is a warning or grace period.

groups.title: Profit Consistency Rule
paragraphs: For a reward claim, no single trading day may account for more than 40% of total accumulated net virtual profit. If the best day exceeds this threshold, additional eligible trading profit may be needed before a claim meets the rule.

groups.title: Pre-Trade Risk Indicator
paragraphs: The order ticket may show a Fail Price or risk indicator estimating where a position could reach an account loss boundary. It is an estimate based on displayed assumptions, not a guarantee. Review it alongside position size, leverage, and account equity before placing an order.

title: Claiming Performance Rewards
summary: Claim Profit requests, eligibility, review, verification, and the separate withdrawal step.

groups.title: Overview
paragraphs: Claim Profit requests transfer eligible simulated performance rewards from a Blastrr Capital simulated funded account to the user's Primary Account. A separate withdrawal is needed to move a Primary Account balance to an external wallet.
A claim is subject to account rules, risk review, current eligibility requirements, and verification. Simulated performance does not guarantee a real-world payout.

groups.title: Claim Flow
items: Submit a Claim Profit request from the account portfolio when eligible; close positions first if required by the platform.
Select an available reward asset if the form offers a choice.
The platform reviews risk limits, trading history, consistency rules, and verification status.
Approved requests are credited according to the current claim process. Withdrawals to external wallets use a separate flow.

rows: Eligibility begins 14 calendar days after the first trade on a simulated funded account.
No single day may exceed 40% of total net virtual profit at claim time.
The account must comply with its Daily Loss Limit and Maximum Drawdown.
Subject to audit and verification; follow the timing shown in the claim flow.

groups.title: Reward Split
paragraphs: The reward split is set by the applicable Blastrr Capital plan and current terms. Review the split shown for your account when submitting a claim; do not assume all plans use the same percentage.

groups.title: Identity Verification
paragraphs: A first reward claim may require identity verification, such as an ID check and selfie, before approval. Subsequent requests follow the verification requirements presented by the platform.

groups.title: Claim Profit vs. Wallet Transfer
paragraphs: Claim Profit moves eligible rewards internally from a simulated funded account to a Primary Account. A wallet transfer moves an available Primary Account balance to an external Web3 address. Check the destination, asset, and network carefully; external blockchain transfers may be irreversible.
